findings.finding: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ n·r where r=LCM(x,y,z)/(x+y+z). Minimal r=6/11 (x=2,y=3) if 11|n; else r=A/D with D=d1d2+d1+d2, A=d1d2. D|n ⇔ D|(c+1) for D∤3. Compute M=3^{2025!}, M≡1(mod D) if 3∤D. For each c, find smallest D∈{d1d2+d1+d2} dividing n, get r=A/D. g(c)=⌊2025!·r⌋/2025! (×5 for c=4M). Sum floors N, g= N/2025!. Reduce p/q=N/gcd(N,2025!)/ (2025!/gcd). (p+q) mod 99991=54680.

f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For n=M=3^k, use (M/9,2M/9,2M/3) ⇒ f=2/3 M, g(0)=2/3. For n=5M, same ⇒ g(4M)=10/3. For n=M+c (c≡2 mod 3), n not div 3 ⇒ any divisor d|c+1 (odd, 3∤d) can be sum. Minimal ratio r(d)=z/d from triples where z multiple of x,y. Best ratios: 6/11 (s=11), 4/7 (s=7), 8/13 (s=13), 10/17 (s=17), 16/25 (s=25), 20/31 (s=31)… Since c+1’s odd part lacks 7,11,13,17, only 25 or 31 etc apply. Compute each c+1 factorization, find smallest divisor d with known pattern → g(c)=r(d). Sum all g’s → p/q → (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure d not multiple of 3, use only odd divisors; g(c)=z/d (no floor needed).

Key: f(n)=n·min_{d1<d2>1, D|n} d1d2/D, D=d1d2+d1+d2. Minimal ratio 6/11 (D=11) iff 11|n; else use smallest D|n from set {11,14,17,20,…}. For M=3^{2025!}, M≡1 mod D (if 3∤D). Compute D|M+c via (c+1) mod D for 3∤D. Found D:27→2/3, 53→34/53, 47→30/47, 197→130/197, 167→110/167; 4M gives 5·2/3=10/3. Sum =540747228/81951409, p+q≡54680 (mod 99991). Pitfall: ensure 2025! divisible by D so floor=exact.

Odd n ⇒ use a=2,b=(n‑2)/p (p=smallest odd divisor of n‑2). For given c (even) n=M+c odd, n‑2 always divisible by 3 ⇒ f=(2/3)(M+c‑2). For c=0,4M use a=1,b=(n‑1)/4 ⇒ f=(3/4)(n‑1). Sum g’s =43/6‑2/N, N=2025!. Reduce → p+q=(49N)/12‑1. Compute N/12 mod 99991: 2025!·12⁻¹≡63098. Answer = (49·63098‑1) mod 99991 = ?

f(N)=min m:∃a<b|m, a+b+m=N ⇒ m=N−a−b, a,b|m. Minimal m from (1,d,m) with d|(N−1), d≤(N−1)/3 ⇒ k=smallest divisor≥3 of N−1, m=(N−1)(k−1)/k. For N=M+ c (M=3^{2025!}), compute k via N−1≡(3^K−1+c) mod p. Results: k(0)=4, k(4M)=4, k(1848374)=11, k(10162574)=9814, k(265710644)=4, k(44636594)=17. g(0)=3/4−1/D, g(4M)=15/4−1/D, others g=(k−1)/k. Sum S=21/4+10/11+9813/9814+16/17−2/D. D=2025!. p+q≡D·33401575−7340872 (mod 99991). D≡57239 (mod 99991) ⇒ answer 93919. Pitfalls: ensure k≠2, handle c=0,4M separately (floor subtracts 1). Use pow(3,K,mod) with K=2025! for small mod.

f(n)=min LCM of 3 divisors ⇒ t=LCM. For n=M+c, t=α·n where α=pq/(pq+p+q) if D=pq+p+q|n (i.e. D|c+1) else α=(p'‑1)/p' with p' smallest odd prime|n‑1. Compute c+1 divisors → best α. Values: g(0)=4/5, g(4M)=1‑1/2025!, g(1848374)=34/53, g(10162574)=21/31, g(265710644)=511/591, g(44636594)=123/167. Sum p+q≡77219 (mod 99991).

Use odd n=M+c. For n odd, f(n)=min{(n‑1)(1‑1/d₁), (n‑2)(1‑1/d₂)} with d₁=smallest divisor>2 of n‑1, d₂ of n‑2. For c=0,4M → d₁=4 ⇒ f=(3/4)(n‑1). For other c, d₂=3 ⇒ f=(2/3)(n‑2). Then g(c)=⌊N·f/M⌋/N gives 3/4‑1/N,15/4‑1/N,2/3. Sum S=43/6‑2/N ⇒ p/q=(43N‑12)/(6N). Reduce by 12: p=43N/12‑1, q=N/2. Compute K=N/12 mod 99991 (K=63098). Answer=49K‑1≡92071. Pitfall: ensure floor subtracts 1 only when constant term negative.
